To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
DEFB103 bidirectional regulates chemokine/cytokine responses to a microbial antigen in human, murine, and in silico dendritic cells.
DEFB103 bidirectly regulates the chemokine response to Porphyromanas gingivalis HagB in dendritic cells and in vivo.

human DEFB103 acts both as a stimulant and attenuator of chemotactic and inflammatory responses to a microbial stimulus, and this dichotomous activity is dependent upon the concentration and time of exposure of DEFB103 to dendritic cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the chemokines and cytokines that orchestrate the inflammatory response, and the mechanisms that regulate these chemokine and/or cytokine responses.
the role of DEFB103 in the regulation of dendritic cell chemokine and/or cytokine responses to microbial stimuli.
the role of DEFB103 in the regulation of the innate immune responses of dendritic cells to P. gingivalis, a periodontal pathogen.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DEFB103 acts bidirectionally in a concentration- and timing-dependent manner to regulate the chemokine, cytokine, and growth factor responses to HagB.
DEFB103 bidrectionally regulates chemokines and cytokines, and that DEFB103 is an important player in the orchestration of host immune responses to microbial pathogens.
DEFB103 is a bidirectional regulator of chemokines and cytokines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DEFB103 can act as either an enhancer or an attenuator of the chemokines and cytokines in the dendritic cell response to a pro-inflammatory bacterial stimulus.
DEFB103 is a dual regulator, which acts as both a chemokine and a cytokine stimulant and attenuator, and that DEFB103 has the capacity to influence the chemokine response in both human and mice.
DEFB103 can act as a stimulant or attenuator of chemotactic and inflammatory activities, and that DEFB103 is a key player in the regulation of chemokines and cytokines.
The main takeaway from our work is that

DEFB103 is not a pro-inflammatory mediator, but rather a modulator of the pro-inflammatory response to microbial antigens, which can either enhance or attenuate the pro-inflammatory response depending on the context of the response.

DEFB103 can act as a pro-inflammatory mediator and as an immunosuppressant, and that the balance between the two activities is determined by the concentration of DEFP103 and the order of timing of exposure to dendritic cell.
DEFB103 has the potential to be a therapeutic target for modulating the chemokine response to P. gingivalis.
